---
title: "Installing Sprout"
description: |
  Install Sprout to use on the command-line and in Python projects.
order: 0
---

Before installing Sprout, you need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed.
To check that it is available, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv --version
```

The command should print a version number. If you get an error instead, install
uv before continuing.

## Install globally

Installing Sprout globally lets you run it from any directory on your machine.
To install globally, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv tool install seedcase-sprout
```

Once installed, you can run the program with `seedcase-sprout` (or `sprout` for
short). Alternatively, use `uvx` to run Sprout without having to separately
install it first---this always fetches the latest version:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uvx seedcase-sprout
```

::: content-hidden
<!-- TODO: unhide after implementing auto-completions -->

To enable shell auto-completions, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-sprout --install-completion
```

::::: callout-note
Completions only work for bash, fish, and zsh shells.
:::::
:::

## Install in a Python project

Installing Sprout in a project's virtual environment keeps its dependencies
contained within the project and not available throughout the system.

We assume you've already created a Python project with a `pyproject.toml` file.
We recommend creating a Python project using our [template data
package](https://template-data-package.seedcase-project.org).

From your project's directory, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv add seedcase-sprout
```

To verify the installation, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv pip show seedcase-sprout
```

If successful, the output will show details about the installed package and
you're now ready to use Sprout in your project!
